name: MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.CAR.exists_unitary_crossRepresentation_path_approx
title: Approximating another vector state along a unitary path

content.display_title: Approximating another vector state along a unitary path
content.one_sentence_role: A fixed irreducible CAR representation can approximate any vector state on finitely many elements by moving a given unit vector.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be the completed CAR algebra: the norm completion of the increasing union of $A_n=M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$ under the unital embeddings $a\mapsto a\otimes I_2$ (with the fixed coordinate reindexing). Write $\iota_n:A_n\to A$ for the canonical isometric inclusion and $e_{ij}^{(n)}=\iota_n(E_{ij})$ for its matrix units. A representation is a unital complex star homomorphism into the bounded operators on a complex Hilbert space. Irreducibility means nonzero action and no proper nonzero closed reducing subspace. We use the inner product conjugate linear in its first argument and write $\varphi_{\pi,v}(a)=\langle v,\pi(a)v\rangle$ for the vector functional. Let $\pi:A\to B(H)$ be irreducible with $H\ne0$, let $\sigma:A\to B(K)$ be any representation, and choose unit vectors $\xi\in H$ and $\eta\in K$. For every finite $F\subset A$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exist a unitary $u\in U(A)$ and a norm-continuous path from $1$ to $u$ such that $|\varphi_{\pi,\pi(u)\xi}(a)-\varphi_{\sigma,\eta}(a)|<\varepsilon$ for all $a\in F$.
content.assumptions: The spaces $H$ and $K$ are complete complex Hilbert spaces. Both representations are unital; only $\pi$ must be irreducible. There are no initial stage-state tests and no protected finite set.
content.conclusion: The approximating state is obtained from the specified starting vector $\xi$ by a unitary in the identity path component of $U(A)$. The approximation is on the prescribed finite set at the endpoint.
content.proof_summary: Keep the given vectors $\xi\in H$ and $\eta\in K$ fixed. Purification supplies a new unit vector $\zeta\in H$ that realizes the target state on a sufficiently large stage $m$. To move $\xi$ to $\zeta$, use the fixed-stage transport lemma at stage $0$, where its tests are automatic. These are two different stages: $m$ controls approximation, whereas stage $0$ supplies transport without any near-centrality requirement.

proof_steps.text: Choose $m$ so that each $a\in F$ has an approximant $b_a\in\iota_m(A_m)$ with $\|a-b_a\|<\varepsilon/3$. Apply [finite-stage purification](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/StagePurification.lean#L256-L278) to the given $\pi$, $\sigma$, and $\eta$ at stage $m$. Its hypotheses hold because $\pi$ is nonzero and irreducible, both representations are unital, and $\|\eta\|=1$. It gives $\zeta\in H$ with $\|\zeta\|=1$ and $\varphi_{\pi,\zeta}(b)=\varphi_{\sigma,\eta}(b)$ for all $b\in\iota_m(A_m)$. This is a new vector; the prescribed starting vector $\xi$ is not replaced.

Use the [fixed-stage exact-transport lemma](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/LocalTransport.lean#L353-L455), not the protected-finite-set theorem. For a prescribed stage $n$ and a positive commutator tolerance, it supplies a $\delta>0$ before the pair of unit vectors is chosen. Its hypothesis compares their vector functionals on the matrix units of that stage. Set $n=0$ and take the auxiliary commutator tolerance to be $1$; its commutator conclusion will not be needed.

The inputs to this transport lemma are $\xi,\zeta\in H$ in the same representation $\pi$, not $\xi$ and $\eta$ from different spaces. Since $A_0=\mathbb C$ and $e_{00}^{(0)}=1$, unitality and the two unit-vector norms give $|\varphi_{\pi,\xi}(e_{00}^{(0)})-\varphi_{\pi,\zeta}(e_{00}^{(0)})|=|1-1|=0<\delta$. This is the only matrix-unit test at stage $0$. Thus the lemma supplies $u$ and a path $p$ from $1$ to $u$ with $\pi(u)\xi=\zeta$. No comparison between these states on the larger stage $m$, and no norm closeness of $\xi$ and $\zeta$, is required.

For each $a\in F$, the two states agree at $b_a$ and are contractive, so $|\varphi_{\pi,\zeta}(a)-\varphi_{\sigma,\eta}(a)|\leq2\|a-b_a\|<2\varepsilon/3<\varepsilon.$ Substitute $\zeta=\pi(u)\xi$ to obtain the asserted endpoint estimate.

content.lean_realization_notes: The conclusion supplies a path but makes no near-centrality claim and no uniform approximation claim along that path. It does not identify the two representations or give exact equality of their states on all elements.
